newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Republicans have 227-205 House edge so far.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Republicans have 227-205 House edge so far.

text.p: As near-final House of Representatives returns trickled in on Thursday, eight days after the election, Republicans appeared to have secured 227 seats and Democrats 205 -- with two still in contention.

The newest returns show California Democratic Representative George Brown winning against Republican Linda Wilde, while Democratic challenger Loretta Sanchez appears to have defeated Republican California Representative Bob Dornan.

Returns were not final in Washington state, but mail ballots gave a comfortable edge to two Republican incumbents, Representative Linda Smith over Democrat Brian Baird and Representative Jack Metcalf over Democrat Kevin Quigley.

Depending on the outcome in two Texas races that will be held next month, the Republican margin over Democrats will be anywhere from 20 to 24 seats. Near the end of the 104th Congress, Republicans held a 37-seat advantage.
An independent from Vermont, who often votes with Democrats, won a single seat in the 435-member House.

In Texas, party control of two seats will be decided in special run-offs on Dec. 10, one between Republican Representative Steve Stockman and Democrat Nick Lampson and the other between Democratic Representative Ken Bentsen and Republican Dolly Madison McKenna.
